analysis:
The supplied units are head-side text from CHANGELOG.md (lines 1645-2127). The patch excerpt shows a documentation-only modification: the v0.10.0 candidate header becomes a v0.10.1 candidate, with upgrade and rollout notes added. The excerpt is truncated, and the supplied text covers only historical changelog entries, not the new v0.10.1 section at head lines 11-138. No code, configuration, or enforcement logic is present in the supplied units, so I found no concrete security regression.

I checked the historical entries against T-041 (prefix-cache leak and TTFT oracle) and the App Attest authorization threats T-052 to T-058. They describe the cache posture as encrypted SSD with authenticated checkpoints, tenant/model/prompt identity gates, a global opt-out, and KEK-rooted keys. These match the canonical threat model and do not claim to loosen the 30-minute TTL, account scoping, or HMAC naming. The App Attest entries keep serving disabled by default and require qualification, which is consistent with TB-011.

The visible rollout notes in the patch excerpt say the release must run behind a coordinator that includes darkbloom-platform#411, which refuses logprobs on certain models. That is an unverified external contract (a coordinator dependency) and is documentation, not evidence of a regression in this repo. It also notes that page-cache accounting changes may count more memory as available. That is a behavioral change in the new section, which I could not see. Integration should check the source behind that claim for T-029/memory-admission effects and for any changes to the T-041 cache posture. The new v0.10.1 text at lines 11-138 was not supplied and needs review where it describes security-relevant changes.
